content:
Florida Sen. Ashley Moody apparently thought Wednesday was a good day to go after the video game “Grand Theft Auto,” only to have her attempt at a “culture war” fail miserably.

The Florida Republican defeated Democratic challenger Angie Nixon earlier this month, one of the GOP’s few highlights during the midterm elections.

Moody tried to consolidate power and unite voters by tweeting against the popular, violent video game, which just released its 6th edition after a 13-year break.

The senator’s main beef with the game? She thinks it makes the Sunshine State seem more lawless than she claims:

At least one person gently tried to let Moody know that ― spoiler alert! ― GTA is just a video game set in a fictional universe.

Others noted that a grand jury report from earlier this year alleged that when Moody was Gov. Ron DeSantis’ attorney general, she was aware his administration “misappropriated” $10 million in taxpayer money and diverted the funds to a charity connected to the governor’s wife.

“Despite our finding that the money was misappropriated, we find insufficient evidence to charge anyone criminally,” the report declared.

One person suggested that “GTA 6” may actually be a prediction of Florida’s future after it passed an amendment that some fear may gut police and firefighter services in some communities.

Of course, Jeffrey Epstein’s name came up...

Other people just shook their heads at just how out of touch Moody’s post was.

A few people wondered if going after Florida’s depiction in a popular video game was the right move for a Republican, considering how voters rejected the party earlier this month.

Moody is not the only person in the conservative industrial complex going after “Grand Theft Auto.”

Fox News personality Rachel Campos-Duffy was accused of engaging in “culture war bullshit” on Wednesday after she suggested on “Fox & Friends” that she was “not thinking this is a good thing for our culture and society.”

HuffPost reached out to Moody’s office for comment on the reactions to her post, but no one immediately responded.
